content: The metabolism of the enzyme CYP3A4 is influenced by various drugs, necessitating careful monitoring and potential therapy adjustments. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drug combinations: 1. Ketoconazole and Darunavir: Both drugs increase each other's effects by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative drugs or avoid co-administration. 2. Ketoconazole and Cobicistat: Ketoconazole raises cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Darunavir and Lacosamide: Darunavir increases lacosamide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and monitor closely. 4. Cobicistat and Lansoprazole: Cobicistat increases lansoprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Darunavir and Lapatinib: Darunavir increases lapatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, adjust the lapatinib dose accordingly. 6. Darunavir and Larotrectinib: Darunavir increases larotrectinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Cobicistat and Lefamulin: Cobicistat increases lefamulin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 8. Darunavir and Lemborexant: Darunavir increases lemborexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Lenacapavir and Darunavir: Lenacapavir increases darunavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Darunavir and Lenolisib: Darunavir increases lenolisib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Darunavir and Letermovir: Letermovir increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat and Levamlodipine: Cobicistat increases levamlodipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema, and adjust the dose if necessary. 13. Darunavir and Levomilnacipran: Darunavir increases levomilnacipran levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Cobicistat and Levonorgestrel (oral): Cobicistat increases levonorgestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Darunavir and Lidocaine: Darunavir increases lidocaine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Darunavir and Linagliptin: Darunavir increases linagliptin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Darunavir and Liraglutide: Darunavir may cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely. 18. Darunavir and Lofexidine: Darunavir increases lofexidine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia, and consider dose reduction. 19. Darunavir and Lomitapide: Darunavir increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious reactions. 20. Darunavir and Lonafarnib: Darunavir increases lonafarnib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Darunavir and Lopinavir: Darunavir increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Darunavir and Loratadine: Darunavir increases loratadine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Darunavir and Lorlatinib: Darunavir increases lorlatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 24. Darunavir and Losartan: Darunavir increases losartan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Darunavir and Lovastatin: Darunavir increases lovastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 26. Darunavir and Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Darunavir increases ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of lumacaftor/ivacaftor when initiating treatment with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 27. Darunavir and Lurbinectedin: Darunavir increases lurbinectedin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50% if co-administration is unavoidable. 28. Darunavir and Macitentan: Darunavir increases macitentan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Darunavir and Maraviroc: Darunavir increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Darunavir and Marijuana: Darunavir increases marijuana levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Darunavir and Mavacamten: Darunavir increases mavacamten levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure. 32. Darunavir and Mavorizxafor: Darunavir increases mavorizxafor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust the dose if necessary. 33. Darunavir and Medroxyprogesterone: Darunavir increases medroxyprogesterone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Darunavir and Mefloquine: Darunavir increases mefloquine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to the risk of increased toxicity. 35. Darunavir and Meperidine: Darunavir increases meperidine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Darunavir and Mestranol: Darunavir increases mestranol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Darunavir and Metformin: Darunavir may cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely. 38. Darunavir and Methadone: Darunavir increases methadone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the methadone dose and monitor closely. 39. Darunavir and Methylprednisolone: Darunavir increases methylprednisolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Darunavir and Metoclopramide (Intranasal): Darunavir increases metoclopramide levels via CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Darunavir and Metoprolol: Darunavir increases metoprolol levels via CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Darunavir and Metronidazole: Metronidazole increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Darunavir and Mexiletine: Darunavir increases mexiletine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Darunavir and Miconazole (Vaginal): Miconazole increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Darunavir and Midazolam (Oral): Darunavir increases midazolam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged sedation or respiratory depression. 46. Darunavir and Midostaurin: Darunavir increases midostaurin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Darunavir and Mifepristone: Darunavir increases mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Darunavir and Miglitol: Darunavir may cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely. 49. Darunavir and Mipomersen: Both drugs may increase hepatic enzyme levels. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 50. Darunavir and Mirtazapine: Darunavir increases mirtazapine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Darunavir and Mirvetuximab Soravtansine: Darunavir increases mirvetuximab levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for increased risk of adverse reactions. This list highlights the importance of understanding drug interactions mediated by CYP3A4 and other metabolic pathways. Always consult a healthcare professional for specific recommendations tailored to individual patient needs.
